newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris crime down for second year in a row.
newsitem.headline: Paris crime down for second year in a row.

text.p: The crime rate in Paris fell for the second year in a row in 1996, shrinking by more than six percent from the previous year, a local official said on Friday.

Philippe Massoni, Paris prefect (government representative), told a news conference the number of crimes and misdemeanours registered fell from 293,400 in 1995 to 275,027 last year. He said this was the lowest since 1979.

Street crime was down the most, falling by 10.74 percent. Break-ins to homes and car theft were down by slightly less. Violence and business crime increased, however, including fraud through stolen cheques or credit cards.
